'''Warren Bicknell Mori''' (born August 8, 1959) is an American computational plasma [[physicist]] and a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Warren Mori|url=https://www.pa.ucla.edu/faculty-websites/mori.html|access-date=2020-07-24|website=www.pa.ucla.edu}}</ref> He was awarded the 2020 [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=2020 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Mori&first_nm=Warren&year=2020|access-date=2020-07-24|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref> for his contributions to the theory and [[Computer simulation|computer simulations]] of non-linear processes in [[Plasma acceleration|plasma-based acceleration]] using [[Kinetic theory of gases|kinetic theory]],<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Fonseca|first1=R. == Early life and career ==
Mori received a [[Bachelor of Science]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1981. He then went to the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA) and obtained a [[Master of Science]] and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (Ph.D.) in 1984 and 1987 respectively.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" /> For his Ph.D. in electrical engineering, Mori was supervised by plasma physicists [[Francis F. Chen]], [[John M. Dawson]] and [[Chandrashekhar J. Joshi]],<ref>Mori, W. B. (1987) [https://www.seas.ucla.edu/plasma/files/Phd%20Thesis/1987_MORi_PhdThesis.pdf Theory and Simulations on Beat Wave Excitation of Relativisitic Plasma Waves], Ph.D. Thesis. </ref> all of whom were noted for winning the [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]]. Mori then remained at UCLA, and has been there ever since. 

Mori was a director of UCLA's Institute for Digital Research and Education.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Warren Mori – Institute for Digital Research and Education|url=https://idre.ucla.edu/people/warren-mori|access-date=2020-07-24|language=en-US}}</ref>  He is currently a director of UCLA's Particle-in-Cell and Kinetic Simulation Software Center<ref>{{Cite web|title=Particle-in-Cell and Kinetic Simulation Software Center – Opportunities|url=https://picksc.idre.ucla.edu/opportunities/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191029234713/https://picksc.idre.ucla.edu/opportunities/|archive-date=2019-10-29|access-date=2020-07-24|website=PICKSC|language=en-US}}</ref> and Plasma Simulation Group.<ref>{{Cite web|title=UCLA Plasma Simulation|url=https://plasmasim.physics.ucla.edu/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200420212642/https://plasmasim.physics.ucla.edu/|archive-date=2020-04-20|access-date=2020-07-24|website=plasmasim.physics.ucla.edu}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Mori is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1997&unit_id=DPP&institution=University+of+California%2C+Los+Angeles|access-date=2020-07-24|website=American Physical Society|language=en}}</ref> and the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]].<ref name=":0" /> 

In 1995, Mori received the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics|International Center for Theoretical Physics]] Medal for Excellence in Nonlinear Plasma Physics by a Young Researcher. He also won the 2016 Advanced Accelerator Concepts Prize of the [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] for "''his leadership and pioneering contributions in theory and particle-in-cell code simulations of plasma based particle acceleration''".<ref>{{Cite web|title=AAC Prize|url=https://sites.google.com/lbl.gov/aac2020/aac-prize|access-date=2020-07-24|website=sites.google.com|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

Mori was awarded the 2020 [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for "''leadership in and pioneering contributions to the theory and kinetic simulations of nonlinear processes in plasma-based acceleration, and relativistically intense laser and beam plasma interactions".''<ref name=":0" />
